newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch down, mkt awaits Dow move.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch down, mkt awaits Dow move.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened down on Monday amid light selling as dealers began to take profits notched up last Thursday and Friday, traders said.

"Right now it's very quiet, there's very little going on, they're watching to see which way Wall Street will go. Prices are really inflated, but few want to let go of their stocks just yet," a floor trader said.

The leading IPC share index was down 9.62 points, or 0.19 percent, at 5,057.41. Trading volume .TV.MX was thin at 970,000 shares, and even that meager total was inflated by cross trades, dealers said.
Dealers said many key blue chips were flat and heayweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), which has the biggest weighting on the IPC, was tipping the market balance downwards.
Telmex was down 15 centavos at 21.45 pesos, in what traders said was an echo of its ADRs, which were off 3/8 at 54-11/16. The Dow Jones was meanwhile down 20.44 points at 8,173.60.
On the broad market, sliders outnumbered gainers by nine to three out of a total of 31 stocks traded in total.
